title: Hash Embedding token-importance Mirror codes
hypothesis: For a collision-heavy hashed vocabulary whose token importance pairs lie on a shared unit-circle orbit, one per-token Givens angle can preserve embedding/task quality while reducing the native Hash Embedding importance state and complete payload.
physical_object: Two shared 32x16 component embedding tables addressed by deterministic independent hashes; 256 logical token embeddings combine the two looked-up rows.
mirror_coordinate: One angle per token generates its two component importance weights as (cos(theta_i), sin(theta_i)); it replaces the native Hash Embedding's two learned per-token importance scalars, while both shared component tables and hash functions remain unchanged.
logical_multiplicity: 256 distinct token embedding functions backed by two shared hash component tables and token-specific importance coordinates.
prior_art_delta: PA58 Hash Embeddings combine vectors from shared pools selected by hash functions with token-specific importance weights. The native hash tables and two independent learned weights per token are mandatory controls; only the importance vector representation changes.

model.hash_function: two deterministic seeded 64-bit mixing functions; seeds are serialized as metadata
methods: native Hash Embedding with two shared 32x16 tables + two learned importance weights per token
shared hash tables + one tied common importance pair for every token
shared hash tables + one common vector multiplied by one scalar per token
shared hash tables + one learned Givens angle per token (Mirror importance code)

teacher.hash_embedding: E_i = cos(theta_i) * T0[h0(i)] + sin(theta_i) * T1[h1(i)] with independent random shared tables T0/T1 and per-token angles. This is a deliberately aligned importance-orbit feasibility fixture.
teacher.task_quality: A fixed 16x16 decoder maps embeddings to token classes; labels and soft targets are generated from teacher embeddings and are held fixed for all methods.
teacher.collision_sensitivity: Report token embedding and decoder quality separately for token IDs sharing a hash pair versus unique pairs.

controls: native Hash Embedding with unrestricted two per-token importance weights
shared hash tables with common tied importance weights
shared hash tables with scalar token gates
shared hash tables with per-token Givens Mirror angles

development.selection_metric: test token-class NLL/top-1 accuracy and embedding NRMSE, with actual payload bytes and collision-stratified errors
development.allowed_tuning: No tuning planned; fixed tables, vocabulary, training schedule and teacher are run once. Implementation corrections rerun development only before fresh access.

fresh.open_gate: Both development worlds: full-table and native-Hash NRMSE <=0.03; Mirror embedding NRMSE <=0.03 and decoder NLL within 0.02 nat / top-1 within 1pp of native Hash; Mirror complete payload <=0.60x full table; Mirror improves NRMSE over tied/scalar controls by >=0.01 at <=1.10x their bytes; native Hash coefficients do not match Mirror within 0.005 NRMSE at <=Mirror bytes; both collision and noncollision strata satisfy quality gate. Otherwise fresh remains sealed.

storage.authority: actual serialized compressed NPZ inference payload bytes after reload
paid_objects: full table or both shared hash component tables
every per-token importance weight, scalar gate or Mirror angle
fixed decoder used for task-quality evaluation, included in each method payload
NPZ names, headers and compression overhead

success_gate: All three fresh worlds meet embedding/task/collision quality, <=60% complete full-table bytes, simpler controls, and exact payload replay.
failure_gate: Mirror misses the complete-payload or quality gate, tied/scalar controls match at comparable bytes, or native Hash importance weights match within 0.005 NRMSE at no greater payload.
boundaries: aligned synthetic vocabulary and frozen decoder only; no language-model or recommender claim
importance teacher is generated from the same unit-circle family as the Mirror code
all shared hash tables, token codes, decoder and hash metadata are charged
256 tokens and fixed updates are not a capacity or scaling claim
